stem:
During a school sports practice, Meera runs 150 m in 30 s, while Arjun runs 100 m in 10 s.
Which calculation correctly compares their speeds to decide who is faster?

options.text: 150 ÷ 30 = 5 m/s and 100 ÷ 10 = 10 m/s, so Arjun is faster
150 > 100, so Meera is faster because she covered more distance
30 > 10, so Arjun is faster because he took less time

teacher.key_rationale: Speed must be compared as distance per unit time because both distances and times differ: 150/30 = 5 m/s and 100/10 = 10 m/s, so Arjun is faster. Option B traps comparing distance alone, C traps comparing time alone, D traps an invalid operation.
